observed_original_abi.calling_convention: __thiscall (ECX carries the receiver and is dereferenced through the single memory operand before any definite write; bare RET with no imm16; no stack word read as an argument)
observed_original_abi.receiver: ECX, read at 0x00970b30 as the base of the single memory operand `dword ptr [ECX + 0x1e8]`; never copied to another register and never written
observed_original_abi.return_semantics: the 32-bit word STORED at receiver+0x1e8, copied bit for bit into EAX and re-typed as a pointer; the sampled callers dereference it
observed_original_abi.return_type_rationale: MODELLED AS A POINTER, ON THE CALLERS' EVIDENCE AND NOT ON THE DERIVED RECORD'S CLASS. The derived ABI record classifies the EAX value `register_class: pointer_like` on a single heuristic (the last value written to EAX) with `confidence: INFERRED` and `corroboration: not_available`, and that heuristic cannot distinguish a loaded word from a computed address - so it is NOT the reason for this type. The reason is that three independently sampled callers, decompiled live, use the result as an ADDRESS: 0x00c4b250 and 0x00c4c090 each load through it at displacement 0x13c, and 0x00c61070 tests it against 0 before loading through it. `void*` is the weakest C type that states that observed use; it names no pointee type, and the pointee's layout is not modelled. The declared return type is spelled `void*` with no space so the validator's declaration regex binds the span, and the machine width (4 bytes) and `void*` (4 bytes on x86-32) agree.
observed_original_abi.locals: none; the body allocates no frame, saves no register and builds no record
observed_original_abi.outgoing_calls: none; the body holds no CALL, no JMP and no indirect transfer

observed_mechanics: 0x00970b30 8b 81 e8 01 00 00 - MOV EAX,dword ptr [ECX + 0x1e8]: ModRM 0x81 is mod=10 (a disp32 follows), reg=000 (EAX), rm=001 (ECX); the disp32 is 0x000001e8.
0x00970b36 c3 - RET: single exit; the callee pops nothing, so stack cleanup is 0 bytes and owned by the caller.
The body is 7 bytes (0x00970b30..0x00970b36) and contains no branch, no call, no flag test, no register save and no loop: the read at +0x1e8 is unconditional, so every entry reads the same word.
The read happens on every entry: no lazy path, no cache, no publication check, no default and no refresh. A published null comes back as a published null.
Nothing is written. The word at +0x1e8 is not modified by this function and neither is any neighbouring word.
Raw bytes at 0x00970b30..0x00970b38, read live from the program database: 8b 81 e8 01 00 00 c3 cc. The 0xcc at 0x00970b37 is INT3 padding between this entry and the next and is NOT part of the body.

semantic_findings: The entry is a receiver-slot getter returning a pointer: one 32-bit load at displacement 0x1e8, one return, no validation, no transformation, no write.
142 direct callsites across 69 distinct caller functions in the committed xrefs export, every one `direct-call`, and 0 edges out of the target. High fan-in of a leaf accessor.

The returned word is used by all three sampled callers as an ADDRESS: two load through it at displacement 0x13c of the pointee and one null-tests it first. That is the evidence for the `void*` return type, and it is independent of the derived record's heuristic `pointer_like` class.

The immediately adjacent entry at 0x00970b10 is this slot's SETTER - one stack argument stored at [ECX+0x1e8] - which makes 0x1e8 a demonstrated read/write slot and fixes the family's thiscall shape on both ends (bare RET here, RET 0x4 there).

knowledgegraph/triage/datarefs-2540f2ca.tsv records no data reference out of 0x00970b30 in either direction, so on this pinned snapshot the target is not reached through a vtable; that matches the body's zero indirect dispatch and the 142/142 direct-call edges.

The derived ABI record's `pointer_like` return class is INFERRED with `corroboration: not_available`; it is consistent with the callers here but is explicitly NOT the reason the model declares a pointer type.
not_claimed: Any name for the word at receiver+0x1e8, and any name for the receiver's class. UNKNOWN; the receiver record is bounds_only and the type above is opaque.

The pointee's type, size or layout. The callers reach at least displacement 0x13c of it; the production header declares no pointee type and the model stops at the pointer. The PointeeFixture is a model-test device, not a recovered layout.
Any writer of the word at +0x1e8 beyond the adjacent setter, and any immutability or publication claim for it.
The receiver's size or layout. 0x1ec is a modelling bound through the one word the body reads, not a recovered allocation size.
Nullability, ownership, AddRef/Release or thread-safety of either the receiver or the returned pointer. The body has no room for a reference call.
Any calling convention other than __thiscall, and any ordinary stack argument for this target. The neighbouring setter's one stack argument belongs to that entry, not this one.
That 0x00970b10 is a separate reconstructed function. It carries no function record in the program database and is cited as decoded adjacent code only.
Any runtime, Wine, trace, differential or OBSERVED-behaviour claim. No runtime evidence exists for this VA: the runtime axis is GATED and unattempted.
confidence: high for the mechanism (two instructions, one displacement, one bare RET, a demonstrated setter for the same slot, and three callers agreeing on pointer use); none for the receiver's class, the slot's name, or the pointee's type
unresolved_questions: Which class is the receiver? Nothing in the pack names it; the record has no namespace, no SDK association and no type. The 142 callers all supply their own ECX and the pack does not say from where.
What does the pointer at receiver+0x1e8 point to, and what is at its displacement 0x13c? Three callers load there and one SDK-independent note names nothing; the pointee's type is UNKNOWN.

Is 0x00970b10 the only writer of the slot, and is the adjacent setter the only such accessor pair? The setter is adjacent in the image, which is an adjacency and not an enumeration of writers elsewhere in the binary.
Why does the adjacent setter also write [ECX+0x9c] with the constant 1 in the same call? That coupling is observed but its meaning is not recoverable from this target's evidence.
Do the 69 distinct callers share one receiver class, or is this slot reachable from more than one type? The fan-in is high and uniform but no witness names the receiver's origin.

focused_test.assertion_style: abort on the first failure; each group names the hypothesis it refutes
coverage: the return is the word STORED at +0x1e8 re-typed as a pointer: not the ADDRESS of that word (the LEA form), not the receiver, not the displacement, not a mask/shift/increment of the value

0x1e8 is a byte displacement and not an index: the planted word at +0x1e4 and the words at +0x000/+0x004 are all different and none is returned, and the disp32-as-element-count reading lands at byte 0x7a0, past the modelled extent
the getter and the adjacent setter name ONE address: pinned at compile time and re-checked at run time, and the setter's OTHER displacement (+0x9c) is shown to be a different byte
the body reads: the whole 0x1ec-byte receiver is byte-identical before and after the call

the bits cross verbatim: 0, 1, 2, 0x7f, 0x80000000, 0xfffffffe, 0xffffffff and a 4x4 sweep of the byte pattern all come back unchanged, so no default, mask, sign-extension or saturation survives; and the sampled callers' POINTER use reproduces - a published null comes back null, and a non-null value is the address the caller then loads through at displacement 0x13c

the ABI is measured, not asserted: ESP is sampled before the call and after the return and must agree (the callee pops nothing), contrasted against the adjacent setter's RET 0x4; the receiver arrives in ECX with nothing pushed; a second receiver at a different address yields a different answer; and the sidecar's 142/69/0 edge counts are pinned

the encoding is the observed seven bytes, ModRM 0x81 decodes as mod=10/reg=EAX/rm=ECX, the disp32 equals the header's displacement, the opcode is 0x8b and not 0x8d (LEA), the tail is a bare 0xc3 and not 0xc2, and the 0xcc pad is named
the entry's literal displacement and the header's kFieldDisplacement name one and the same address

A mutation counts as detected only when the build fails or the binary aborts. The unmutated baseline was rebuilt and re-run before the batch and passes.
